summary: Three separate security incidents were identified. An external IP performed port scanning and a suspected SQL injection attack against the public web server, potentially exfiltrating data. A phishing email led to the compromise of Ayesha Malik's account, followed by a VPN login from an unusual location and a large data transfer from the finance file server. The internal firewall log was unavailable for a period, potentially hiding further internal activity during the credential compromise. Two other activities were identified as approved vulnerability scanning and remote desktop for patching.

suspected.text: The connection from LT-FIN-014 to orbit-payroll-verify.example is suspected to be Ayesha Malik clicking the phishing link.
suspected.assumption: The connection from Ayesha Malik's laptop to the phishing link domain indicates the user clicked the link.

suspected.text: The VPN login by amalik from Romania (198.51.100.77) after multiple MFA push denials is suspected to be an attacker using Ayesha Malik's compromised credentials.
suspected.assumption: Multiple rejected MFA pushes followed by an approved push from a new country is treated as a sign of a stolen password.

suspected.text: The Kerberos TGT request, service ticket requests for SRV-FS01 and SRV-DB01, and the password reset attempt for amalik from the VPN assigned IP 10.10.3.45 are suspected to be actions by the attacker using the compromised amalik account.
suspected.assumption: The VPN session from an unusual location is attributed to an attacker, therefore subsequent activity from that VPN IP using the same account is also attributed to the attacker.

suspected.text: The large data transfer from SRV-FS01 to the attacker's VPN session is suspected to be data exfiltration.
suspected.assumption: A large transfer of data from a sensitive file server to an attacker-controlled VPN session is indicative of data exfiltration.

suspected.text: The large 200 response to the SQL injection query '/orders/search?id=-1%20UNION%20SELECT%20NULL,username,password%20FROM%20users--' is suspected to indicate successful data extraction from the database.
suspected.assumption: A large 200 response to an attack request may mean success.

insufficient.text: The SRV-FS01 file access (audit) log is not collected, so it is unknown which specific files were read during the large data transfer.
The SRV-DB01 login and query log is not collected, so it is unknown what specific queries were executed or data accessed on the database server.

The internal firewall log is missing for the period 06:32:00 to 07:28:59 UTC, so any internal network activity by the attacker using amalik's account via VPN (10.10.3.45) during this time is not visible.
